text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- President Boris Yeltsin's statement that Russia would not accept Finnish NATO membership was no surprise to Finland, says foreign minister Tarja Halonen.
- Finnish cadets on survival training in Lapland find shelter against snowstorms in the snow.
- High-school graduation tests starting today with native language essays. @
- Cold and snowfall to return to southern Finland after a spell of spring weather.
- Opticians testing drivers' sight at petrol stations.
- MP Pertti Virtanen using taxpayers' money for subscriptions to comics, such as spiderman and Tex Willer.
- European Union still lacks Finnish interpreters.
- Helsinki bartenders have created drinks in honour of the U.S.-Russia summit with such names as Bill, Boris and Mara.
- Daily goods wholesaler and retailer Kesko plans to start banking service by allowing money withdrawals with client cards. Testing to start this spring in Raahe and Lahti. @
KAUPPALEHTI
- Merita, Orion, Kone and Finnair are now the only groups among the 30 largest listed companies not to have options schemes to set incentives for their managements.

- Brokerages may still have to lower their fees amid tough competition, from between 0.1 and 0.3 percent last year which is about half of the level three years ago. Higher volumes patch up some losses but costs are rising too. @
- Bank of Finland director Esko Ollila does not expect the group of cooperative banks to be shattered although some local banks may choose not to take part in tighter cooperation around OKOBANK.
- Car dealers must be careful not to pay too much for used cars in exchange for new ones, says Matti Porho, chairman of the car dealers' association. @
AAMULEHTI
- Public-sector efforts to boost efficiency through privatisation, competition and civil servants' accountability for profits ups the risks of corruption, dissertation says.
- The four leading steel wholesalers are becoming leaders in trade via computer networks.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Abolition of lease regulation since 1992 has boosted supply by some 50,000 flats, making renting a real alternative to ownership. @
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET
- Boris Yeltsin's statement that Russia would accept Finnish NATO membership was clumsy, unskilled and undiplomatic, says U.N. human rights envoy and NATO-link advocate Elisabeth Rehn.
- Interbank's CEO Paavo Prepula warns that leveraged speculators are again active on the securities market.
